findings.title: Redis OSS 5.0.5 replication group is in paid Extended Support
findings.description:
aws_elasticache_replication_group.kong (redis.tf:1) sets engine = "redis" (redis.tf:7) and engine_version = var.redis_engine_version (redis.tf:8), whose default is "5.0.5" (variables.tf:487). Redis OSS 5 left standard support on 2026-01-31. In Extended Support since 2026-02-01. Next price step 2027-02-01 (Year 2, same 80% premium); Year 3 at 160% from 2028-02-01. EOL 2029-01-31; after that AWS upgrades remaining caches to the latest Valkey. 5.0.5 is deprecated and the live cache most likely runs 5.0.6 (not confirmed: live data unavailable). The cache is created only when var.enable_redis = true (default false, variables.tf:473), so whether it is deployed is unknown. Estimated exposure ~$40 per month (estimate, 2 x cache.t2.small, assumed us-east-1; see https://aws.amazon.com/elasticache/pricing/). Risk Medium (3): automatic failover / Multi-AZ off (+2), no staging environment found (+1). Recommended Valkey 9.1. Alternatives: Valkey 8.2, Valkey 7.2 (rollback path), Redis OSS 7.1 (avoids the TLS blocker). Confirm that cache.t2.small is offered for the chosen Valkey version in your Region.

findings.title: In-transit encryption is off; a Valkey target needs a TLS decision
findings.description: transit_encryption_enabled is not set on aws_elasticache_replication_group.kong, so in-transit encryption is off. Valkey replication groups require TransitEncryptionEnabled at creation (CloudFormation docs, cfn-lint); whether an in-place engine change also requires it is not confirmed. Enabling TLS changes how Kong connects. Proposed manual change: either enable TLS (transit_encryption_enabled = true with transit_encryption_mode = "preferred" first, then "required") and update Kong's Redis SSL settings, or choose Redis OSS 7.1 (target C). The remediation will not set it automatically.

findings.title: Kong rate-limiting counters and caching use the Redis cache
findings.description: The cache is provisioned for Kong rate-limiting counters and caching. Counters and cached data are kept through the upgrade; connections drop during failover. Confirm the plugin's Redis timeout/fault-tolerance settings, test against valkey/valkey:9, and set the plugin's Redis SSL option if TLS is enabled.

findings.title: Clients use the primary endpoint DNS name (no hard-coded IPs)
findings.description: The primary endpoint address is published to SSM (/<service>/<environment>/redis/primary-endpoint) and no hard-coded node IPs were found. The endpoint DNS name is unchanged by the upgrade. No change needed.

findings.title: No TLS client configuration for Redis
findings.description: The (commented) DECK_REDIS_HOST wiring and the rest of the repository show no rediss:// or TLS settings. If transit encryption is enabled for a Valkey target, Kong's Redis connections must be switched to TLS first.

findings.title: Custom parameter group on family redis5.0
findings.description: aws_elasticache_parameter_group.kong uses family var.redis_family, default "redis5.0" (variables.tf:494), with no parameter overrides. Its family must change with the target (valkey9, valkey8, valkey7 or redis7); there are no static values to carry over.

findings.title: Cache is optional (enable_redis defaults to false); deployment not verified
findings.description: The replication group uses count = var.enable_redis ? 1 : 0 and enable_redis defaults to false. Without live data it is unknown whether any environment deploys it. Assessed from IaC only.
